title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.1–6 of this 1986 'Analysis situs' draft): M is a set of 'multiplicités/strates' carrying two order relations, ≤ (incidence) and a finer relation ≪. L ⊂ M is the subset of 'lieux' (places, the point-like strata). 𝔉 is a set of 'figures'; each figure F has a set F̃ of strata. Fig(M) ⊂ 𝔓𝔓(M) denotes 'figures ensemblistes' in M, i.e. families of subsets of M, possibly indexed. On the previous page Grothendieck defines two maps. (1.6a) sends F to Omb_M(F), the 'big shadow' of F. For a single element X it is Omb(X) = {Y ∈ M | Y ≪ X}, a down-set for ≪. (1.6b) sends F to Multomb_M(F) = (Omb X)_{X ∈ F̃}. He notes that (1.6a) need not be injective, while (1.6b) is.

This page names Multomb(F) the 'grande multiombre' (M-multiombre) of F. In modern terms it is a set-theoretic figure in M, i.e. a family of subsets of M indexed by the strata F̃ of F, and it determines F. This is plausible: if X ↦ Omb(X) is injective, which holds since ≪ is an order and principal down-sets determine their generators, then the family recovers F̃ and hence F.

He then brings in the inclusion L ↪ M and the inverse-image maps 𝔓(M) → 𝔓(L) (Z ↦ Z ∩ L) and Fig(M) → Fig(L) (componentwise intersection with L). Composing gives (1.9):
- (a) omb(F) = Omb(F) ∩ L, the 'petite ombre', i.e. the set of places (lieux) of F. This map has no reason to be injective.
- (b) multomb(F) = (Omb(X) ∩ L)_{X ∈ F̃}, the '(petite) multiombre'. It 'tends to be' injective.

The next page states the reconstruction claim: figures are almost never recovered from their shadow, but they are recovered from their multishadow in the case of 'ateliers ensemblistes'. The prototype is an abstract simplicial complex or regular cell complex. The shadow is its vertex set, which loses everything. The multishadow is the family of vertex sets of its cells, with incidence given by inclusion, which recovers the complex.

The problem served: setting up an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs' (a tame/stratified geometry) in which figures are encoded by point-sets of places, generalizing set systems of vertices.
errors: No mathematical error. The claim that Multomb(F) determines F relies implicitly on X ↦ Omb(X) being injective on strata and on F being determined by F̃. Both are reasonable given the definitions on p.4, but neither is argued here.

'A tendance à l'être' for (1.9b) is deliberately vague; injectivity of the small multishadow needs a hypothesis (e.g. every stratum determined by the places below it, as in 'ateliers ensemblistes'). This is acknowledged only informally on p.6.

ideas.what: Big shadow and big multishadow of a figure: down-set in M under ≪, and the family of down-sets of its strata, the latter determining the figure
ideas.modern_name: Encoding a stratified object by the down-closures of its strata in the poset of strata (Alexandrov-topology / face-poset description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (face posets of cell complexes; Alexandrov 1937 for finite topologies)
ideas.where_published: Unsure; the analysis situs drafts of 1986 are unpublished, though tame topology is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Small shadow omb(F) = places meeting F, and small multishadow obtained by pulling back along L ↪ M; the former non-injective, the latter injective for 'set-theoretic workshops'
ideas.modern_name: Vertex set versus vertex-scheme of a (regular) cell / simplicial complex; reconstruction of a complex from the set system of cell vertex-sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard combinatorial topology (abstract simplicial complexes as set systems)

missed.claim: The precise condition under which the small multishadow F ↦ multomb(F) is injective is left open: 'a une tendance à l'être', promised 'Nous y reviendrons'. In effect this asks to characterize when stratified figures are determined by the point-sets (in L) of their strata.
missed.quote: dont la première n'a aucune raison d'être injective, la seconde par contre a une tendance à l'être
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mildly relevant to reconstruction of stratified / tame spaces from combinatorial data, e.g. face posets and exit-path posets. Specialists know the regular-CW and simplicial cases, so little would be new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational bookkeeping in an unpublished axiomatic analysis situs: definitions of 'ombre/multiombre' via pullback along places ↪ strata. It is historically interesting as documentation of Grothendieck's 1986 tame-topology program, but the mathematics is routine (down-sets in a poset, vertex-schemes of complexes).
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2: 'Multomb(F) (est appelée) la grande multiombre de F, i.e. la M-multiombre de F' – the struck word after Multomb(F) is a deletion, and 'est appelé[e]' is the insertion.

'C'est un fait une figure un[?] multiplicité[?] de, M' should read approximately 'C'est en fait une figure ensembliste dans M', with the inserted line 'indexée par F̃ (l'ensemble des strates de F)'. Compare p.6: 'elle est indexée par l'ensemble F̃, ensemble des strates de F'.
Struck circled sentence: 'Jusqu'à présent il n'était pas question de L.'; then 'Utilisant maintenant l'application L ↪ M' (with 'd'autre part' struck and 'maintenant' inserted).
(1.9) left-hand sides are 𝔉 (written F with a stroke), i.e. 𝔉 → 𝔓(L) and 𝔉 → Fig(L).
Last lines read: 'On appellera omb(F) la petite ombre de F, ou simplement son ombre quand une confusion semble exclue, et on parlera aussi de multomb, la (petite) multiombre de la figure F.'
